lesson_title: The CRJ: One Line, Two Truths
hook_text: Every till sale writes TWO numbers — and one of them isn't money.
clip_script: Saturday: R1 500 in the till from the day's sales. That is the money truth — into the money columns. But walk to the shelf: the goods that left had cost Thabo something. His shop marks everything up by 25 percent on cost, so goods that sold for R1 500 went onto the shelf at R1 200. To find that number, do not take 25 percent off — that is the classic slip. Reverse the mark-up: R1 500 divided by 1,25 equals R1 200. And look what the pair of numbers hands Thabo free of charge: R1 500 in, R1 200 off the shelf — he made R300 gross profit today, and he knows it today, not at year end.
visual_style: A till and a shelf side by side: the till glowing green with R1 500 while the shelf dims by R1 200, a R300 badge minting between them; a red X flashes over the 'take 25% off' trap.
pacing: Quick till moment, deliberate slow-down on the divide-by-1,25 move, snap payoff on the R300.
